clue.text: Get one's teeth into gold, by the way

indicators.note: into says the biting phrase goes inside the word for gold

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
to get one's teeth into something is to bite it

explanation.surface: Someone sinks their teeth into gold, perhaps testing a coin, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: OBITER is Latin for 'by the way', familiar from obiter dictum, a judge's remark made in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter is a Latin adverb meaning incidentally or in passing, as in an obiter dictum.

clue.text: Is US currency short here?

parts.note: dollars are bucks, and Bucks is the standard short form of this English county's name

explanation.walkthrough: Buckinghamshire is an English county northwest of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucks is the abbreviation of this county, also American slang for dollars.

clue.text: The restraint, which it contains …

parts.note: taken as written
a rein is a strap that restrains a horse

explanation.surface: A restraint, and what is held inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein means in that place or thing, describing what something holds.

clue.text: … put on the body politic to restore what's been lost?

indicators.note: put on means placed above, so this part comes after in a down entry

parts.note: the state is the body politic
the state is the body politic

explanation.surface: Restraint imposed on a nation in order to bring back what has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue, whose restraint supplies the first piece; 'put on' places it on top in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to bring something back into its former place or condition.

clue.text: Pity lone composer no longer fashionable

indicators.note: something out of fashion is out of its proper form, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: We feel sorry for a lonely composer whose music has fallen out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer' wants to be a musician; here it is a typesetter, one who composes type, and the Linotype was a hot-metal typesetting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing a composer sets type, and the Linotype machine did exactly that work.

clue.text: Falling behind with winter weather precautions

definitions.meaning: insulation wrapped round pipes and tanks against frost

explanation.definitionFit: The word means trailing behind and is also insulating material round pipes against freezing.

clue.text: Carer is out at sunrise, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the remaining letters may be arranged another way
out means the letters of the word is leave the following word

explanation.surface: A carer leaves the house at dawn, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes I and S from SUNRISE, leaving SUNRE, which 'perhaps' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse looks after the sick, so is one who gives care.

clue.text: Old president keeps iron and a more delicate material

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the iron symbol sits within the president's name

parts.note: William Howard Taft was US president 1909-13
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former president holds on to an iron and some finer cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a fine crisp silk fabric, lighter than everyday cloth.

clue.text: Scientist — one gone all too crazy in bygone times?

definitions.meaning: a researcher in a field of science

definitions.text: one gone all too crazy in bygone times?
definitions.meaning: someone obsessed with prehistoric ages, as fossil hunters are

explanation.definitionFit: This scientist studies fossils and so spends a career absorbed in ancient eras.

clue.text: Cultivating plots?

parts.note: reads like tending garden plots, but means fostering secret plans

explanation.definitionFit: Hatching conspiracies is plotting, so a person cultivating plots is conniving.

clue.text: Once confutes what otherwise feels right

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Something that feels right in another way refutes an old argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic word: to refel is an old verb meaning to refute. 'otherwise' gives a rearrangement of the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Refel is an obsolete verb meaning to disprove or refute an argument.

clue.text: Pleasant resort

definitions.meaning: a holiday town on the French Riviera

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means agreeable, and the same spelling is the French Riviera city.

clue.text: Southwest always keeps fine, unusual for disease

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the shuffled word goes between the two outer pieces

parts.note: SW is the compass abbreviation for southwest
ever means always

indicators.note: unusual signals that the following word's letters appear in a strange order

explanation.surface: The southwest of England always enjoys fine weather, which is unusual for a place with disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southwest' looks like a region with fine weather; it is just two compass letters, and 'unusual' rearranges the word for fine weather into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an influenza strain that originated in pigs, so it is a named illness.

clue.text: Toeless sort of boot and a country in Africa

indicators.note: toeless means the tip at the end of the word is cut off

parts.note: Ugg is a brand of sheepskin boot
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of boot with the toe cut off, and a country in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toeless' cuts the last G from UGG, the sheepskin boot, leaving UG.
explanation.definitionFit: Kampala is the capital of this East African nation on Lake Victoria.

clue.text: Spooner's widespread profits for energy suppliers

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: mass means widespread, as in mass appeal
gains are profits

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism tells of huge profits made by energy companies.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of MASS GAINS to get GAS MAINS; the swap is by sound, so the doubled S drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas mains are the large pipes that carry fuel supplies to homes and businesses.

clue.text: Wickedness — it's completely keeping us bunged up

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the pronoun goes inside the combined pieces

parts.note: sin is wickedness
it's written in full is IT IS
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sin keeps us stuffed up, it says.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: sinusitis is the condition that leaves one bunged up.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed sinuses cause a blocked nose, the condition of feeling stuffed up.

clue.text: God — the one not ending where all the others are?

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds
taken as written

indicators.note: not ending means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the word one

explanation.surface: A god asks whether the one deity who never ends lives where all the other gods are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ending' trims ONE to ON. The definition plays on the clue's god: a pantheon is the temple where all the gods are.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is a temple of all the gods, or the gods collectively, so the rest are there.

clue.text: Gentleman's gentleman rises at 4 in the Middle East

indicators.note: rises in a down entry means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's personal manservant
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A butler gets up at four o'clock somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is a large Israeli city on the Mediterranean coast, so it lies in that region.

clue.text: Simpletons perish amid approving gestures

indicators.note: amid means among, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: nods are gestures of approval
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: Fools die while everyone nods in approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A noddy is an old word for a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Nerve cell freshman called for

indicators.note: called means spoken, so the clue's phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: fresh man read as new plus a man's name, Ron

explanation.surface: A nerve cell asks for a new student by name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshman' splits into NEW (fresh) and RON (a man), which spoken together match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a cell that transmits nerve impulses in the body.

clue.text: Dicky urged on to suffer

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky is pushed on into suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name; it is British slang for shaky or unsound, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or endure it.

clue.text: Please sand slippery walkways

indicators.note: slippery suggests the letters slide about into a new order

explanation.surface: A request to put sand on icy paths so people do not fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Esplanades are long open promenades for walking, often along a seafront.

clue.text: Material for a negligee — some wouldn't be seen in one

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a run inside the words

explanation.surface: A see-through nightdress fabric is something you would not wish to be spotted in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a sheer lightweight silk or voile fabric used for lingerie.

clue.text: Decrease in work by a GP

parts.note: a GP is a doctor, DR
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A family doctor's workload goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a fall or reduction in quantity or level.

clue.text: Rustic building with 5 nails

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are assembled anew

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A country cottage put up with five nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustic' looks like it describes the building; it is the definition, and 'building' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Silvan describes woodland and country places, so it means rural or pastoral.

clue.text: Get together when graduate finals are often held?

definitions.text: when graduate finals are often held?
definitions.meaning: a three-year degree of three terms a year ends in the ninth term

explanation.surface: Students mingle at the time when final exams usually fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into IN TERM IX: the ninth term is the last of a three-year British degree with three terms a year.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermix is to mingle together, so things combined in this way come together.

clue.text: Remains after chops start?

indicators.note: start here means the opening letter of the word goes

parts.note: cleavings are things chopped or split apart

explanation.surface: What is left over once someone begins chopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: what remains after the start of CLEAVINGS goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavings are leftovers, the scraps that remain afterwards.

clue.text: Holds forth about right to secede from Brussels

indicators.note: to secede from means to break away, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: Brussels sprouts, the vegetable

explanation.surface: Someone lectures on the right wing breaking away from the European Union in Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brussels' wants to be the EU capital; it is the first half of Brussels sprouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to speak at length and pompously, much like orating.
